hypothesis: Complex bodies (parts, eyes, paddles) emerge but always collapse in small single-niche worlds (per NOTES.md and crown-and-replication.json). Two candidate incubators tested: OCEAN (large single population, tests whether genetic drift in small populations is the killer) and ARCHIPELAGO (three lagoons joined by narrow straits, tests whether island refugia let complexity survive local collapse and reseed).

protocol.bootstrap: viewport forced to 1280x720 (R===334 verified after each load/reload); paused=true; versusSeeds/heirSeeds/dynasty/parentDish reset before every initWorld; sterile (no hand-created creatures in measured runs); page reloaded periodically between runs.
protocol.executionNote: The javascript_tool has a hard ~30s per-call timeout (not the up to 600000ms assumed going in). Ocean seeds happened to finish full 120-minute runs (432000 steps) in single calls (20.3-25.9s each). Archipelago runs consistently exceeded 30s, so from seed 9002 onward each run was executed as a sequence of smaller chunked step() calls against persistent in-page state (window.__rt), with world state never touched between chunks -- purely an execution-mechanics change, not a protocol or determinism change. All 8 seeds reached the full 432000-step / 120-minute target; no seed needed the 60-minute fallback.

fieldDefinitions.withParts: creatures with sg.length>0 (>=1 body segment beyond the head)
fieldDefinitions.branched: withParts creatures where some segment o has o.par!==index-1 or o.ang!==0 (a body fork), matching the game's own 'first branch' detection logic
fieldDefinitions.paddlers: withParts creatures with a segment where o.ang!==0 and o.fin>0.5
fieldDefinitions.eyed: withParts creatures with a segment where o.eye>0.4 (checked independently of branched/paddler status -- confirmed against the archived crown run, e.g. min126: eyed 26 >> branched 7)
fieldDefinitions.mouthed: withParts creatures with a segment where o.mouth>0.4
fieldDefinitions.hidden: count of living creatures with bh>0 (at least one evolved hidden brain neuron)
fieldDefinitions.completeAnimalBar: maxParts>=2 AND eyed/pop>=25% AND paddlers>0, evaluated at a single sample, per the report brief

trial1_ocean.description: initWorld('ocean', SEED); 120 min / 432000 steps target, sampled every 21600 steps (20 samples/seed). 120 founders, 4200 initial algae (vs 50-70 founders / 1800 algae for classic).

summary.noteOnPopulationHypothesis: The 'populations 300+' premise did not materialize at any of the 80 sampled points (min6-120 across 4 seeds); max single sample was 49. A large founder/algae boom does happen in the first simulated minute (observed informally at ~150-166 by 2 sim-seconds in a calibration run) but busts hard before the first 6-minute sample, converging to a population range statistically indistinguishable from (slightly below) the classic baseline (22.6 vs 24.4 avg).

trial2_archipelago.description: initWorld('arch', SEED); 120 min / 432000 steps target, sampled every 21600 steps (20 samples/seed). 3 lagoons x 24 founders = 72 founders, 1800 initial algae. Per-lagoon {pop,withParts,eyed} recorded each sample via lagoonOf(c.x,c.y) on living creatures. archMigration() runs every 60 steps in-engine, allowing individuals to cross straits between lagoons.

summary.noteOnReseedingDefinitions: Definition A (literal, per protocol wording: withParts_i 0->reappears while another lagoon has structure) fires very frequently because per-lagoon populations are tiny (1-17 individuals), so it is dominated by single-individual sampling noise. Definition B (stricter: pop_i itself hits true 0, an unambiguous local wipeout only reversible by cross-strait migration since dead lagoons cannot reproduce locally) is the scientifically load-bearing signal and is reported as primary; A is kept for completeness since the brief specified it literally.
summary.noteOnSmallPopulations: Arch's overall avg pop (16.6) is lower than both classic (24.4) and ocean (22.6) as expected from splitting founders across 3 lagoons -- any refugia benefit has to show up as persistence/survival, not raw counts, exactly as anticipated.

crownRun_60606_180Min.goldenAgeWindow: eyed% stayed >=85% from min54 to min144 (a ~90 minute run, peaking 100% at several samples), then collapsed to 0% eyed by min162 and stayed collapsed through min180 despite population and generation count continuing to climb.

verdict: Refugia (archipelago) shows real, if modest, benefit for persistence; population size alone (ocean) does not help and the 'large population' premise itself was not achieved in practice. See chat report for full paragraph.
